instruction: CLI-only OpenSCAD quantified CAD optimization task. Work from /home/user/Desktop/starter.scad, /home/user/Desktop/baseline.stl, and /home/user/Desktop/constraints.json. Use OpenSCAD command-line modeling and export, not a GUI. Edit /home/user/Desktop/starter.scad or create a derived OpenSCAD source file, then export the final geometry as STL. This is a continuous-score optimization task, not a request to match one hidden answer. Case: wide electronics cover with sparse reinforcing lattice. Objective: Maximize protected footprint per material volume for a thin electronics cover. Hard constraints: keep the final STL within envelope [90.0, 65.0, 18.0] mm, keep each bounding-box span at least [86.0, 61.0, 10.0] mm, keep material volume between 22000.0 and 46000.0 mm^3, and keep the required base/contact footprint usable. Optimize for this evaluator metric after hard constraints are checked: (bbox_x_mm * bbox_y_mm) / volume_mm3; covering more board footprint with less material receives a higher score. Required outputs: /home/user/Desktop/optimized.stl and /home/user/Desktop/design_summary.json. The benchmark evaluates the real exported STL geometry. Do not read or copy ground_truth, do not edit eval.py, and do not fabricate metric files without producing a valid STL.
